rv.q: The experience dominating the minutes spent in the intimate confines of Red Tape Theatre’s storefront stage is that of engagement generated by a multimedia collage.

But muddling time and place doesn’t dim Abdi’s kinetic performance, which captures the furthest reaches of human emotion—from the bubbly joy of first love, to the deep, cold terror of being betrayed by your own family.
With stories told like this, My Name is Inanna restores faith in the future of SWANA representation by reminding our community to 'hold onto hope, remember your name, and wear your crown high.'

cn.t: Critics praise this timely blend of ancient mythology and contemporary Iranian activism, with reviewers highlighting its innovative storytelling and significant contribution to SWANA representation on stage.
